title: Missing Number
pattern: XOR every index with every value
statement: `nums` contains `n` **distinct** numbers taken from the range `0 … n`, so exactly one number of that range is missing. Return the missing number.

example.why: The range is 0 … 3, and 2 is the only number that does not appear.

idea: Imagine two lists: all the numbers `0 … n`, and the values in `nums`. Every number except the missing one appears in **both** lists.
XOR cancels pairs (`a ^ a = 0`). So XOR-ing both lists together cancels everything that is present, and only the missing number survives.
The loop supplies the indexes `0 … n − 1` and the values; the remaining number `n` is put in as the starting value.

complexity.timeWhy: One pass over the array, with two XOR operations per index.

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [3,0,1]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
The full range is 0 … 3. The loop will XOR in the indexes 0 … 2, so start with the one number it never visits: `missing_num` = **3**.
XOR in the index 0 and the value 3: 3 ^ 0 ^ 3 = **0**. Any number that has been put in **twice** (once from the range, once as a value) has cancelled out.
XOR in the index 1 and the value 0: 0 ^ 1 ^ 0 = **1**.
XOR in the index 2 and the value 1: 1 ^ 2 ^ 1 = **2**.
All indexes 0 … 3 and all values have been XOR-ed together. Every number present cancelled itself; what is left is the missing one: **2**.
Done — the answer is **`2`**. The range is 0 … 3, and 2 is the only number that does not appear.
